findings.finding: The FY26 adj. EBITDA guide of EURm 35-40 needs EURm 20-25 in H2 (12-40% y/y) after an H1 of EURm 15.0 (40% of the midpoint) that included a 26% Q2 EBITDA miss against consensus. Q3 is the first test, so the Q3 release decides whether the guide is reiterated or narrowed toward the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Observed report days (dates from the Nasdaq feed, closes from Yahoo): Q2 2026 reiterated after a 26% EBITDA miss, -9.5% (-13.6% over two days). Q3 2025 narrowed the range within the original guide, +6.7%. FY2025/first FY26 guide, +4.7%. Q1 2026 reiterated, -1.8%. Q3 2024, -10.7%
findings.original_quote: Ledelsen har signaleret en indtjeningsprofil som i 2025, hvor andet halvår bidrog med knap 60 % af årets justerede EBITDA, men det kræver fortsat en vækst i andet halvår på 12 til 40 % år over år. Q3 bliver dermed den første reelle test af, om marginløftet materialiserer sig i det tempo, guidance forudsætter. (Management has signalled an earnings profile like 2025's, when H2 contributed just under 60% of the year's adjusted EBITDA, but that still requires 12-40% y/y growth in H2. Q3 is therefore the first real test of whether the margin lift arrives at the pace the guidance assumes.)
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public and the stock is already down 16.9% over 60 days and 4.95% over 20 days (about 3 points of the 20-day fall is the DKK 3.00 ex-dividend on 29 Oct). So the risk of a low-end narrowing is partly priced. What is not priced is the outcome itself. The guide was reiterated right after a big miss, and the share has since drifted lower rather than collapsing, which looks like a market waiting for Q3 rather than one that has written the guide down. A market that had already priced a cut would show a gap down after Q2 that kept going, or broker cuts below the guide; neither was found.
findings.independence: The company's own H1 figures give the same H2 load: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bbbcee02c46d9de71964ff757c3969ed2&lang=en&src=listed . findings.finding: Columbus, a Danish private-sector ERP/IT-services peer, cut its FY26 EBITDA margin guide from 8-10% to about 6% on 22 Oct, citing low H1 activity and a restructuring for AI-driven delivery. That is a negative read on the private-sector half of Trifork's revenue and on Services margins.

findings.why_not_priced: Out for a week, and Trifork's price has not moved on it (100.0-100.5 DKK through 23-28 Oct). It is a narrow proxy: Columbus's Q3 revenue growth actually accelerated to 6% and the cut is mostly restructuring cost, so the transmission to Trifork is weak.

findings.finding: Capital return and balance sheet: EURm 16.0 of Labs proceeds arrived in Q3, the EUR 10m buyback runs weekly, a 2.5% share cancellation started on 30 Sep and the EGM widened the cancellation authority to 10%. Q3 net debt should come down visibly from EURm 21.5 (Q1).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Labs/Verdane announcement on 16 Jul was the last capital-return surprise; no clean read of the reaction was taken
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: every element has been announced. What is left is a possible new buyback once the current EUR 10m programme ends, and a 10% cancellation authority only makes sense if more buying is planned. That second programme is not announced and could plausibly come with the Q3 release or at the CMD.

findings.finding: The CEO (founder Jørn Larsen) sold small blocks of shares right up to the edge of the 30-day MAR closed period: 2,377 shares at DKK 106.57 on 15-17 Sep and 2,472 at DKK 101.64 on 28-30 Sep, about DKK 0.25m each. After Q2 his holding company had bought 10,000 shares at DKK 106 (18-20 Aug) and the chair 9,086 at DKK 110 (26 Aug).
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public but tiny, and the CEO sells in small regular blocks (he also sold 14,735 shares on 24-25 Aug, two days before the chair bought). This looks like routine liquidity selling, not information, so it is sized near zero. One web summary called the 1 Oct filing a purchase; the document says 'Sale'.

findings.finding: Hardware is loaded into H2. H1 2026 hardware revenue was EUR 5.6m against 10.35m in H1 2025, and management expects 'at least the same level of hardware revenues as in 2025' for the full year, with delivery on an announced contract due in Q3 or Q4. Q3 revenue therefore depends on timing, at low margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 headline organic growth was 0% (8% ex-hardware) and the stock fell 1.8%. Hardware timing has repeatedly blurred the headline
findings.why_not_priced: The timing is unknowable before the release, so it is a source of headline revenue noise in either direction, not a sign. Low-margin hardware barely moves the EBITDA guide line.

baseline_tension: The slight negative lean agrees with the run-up (-4.95% over 20 days, about 3 points of it the ex-dividend; -16.9% over 60 days). It does not contradict a positioning signal, because there is none (truncated zero, no anchor). The de-rating since Q2 means a clean reiteration could squeeze upward, which is why p_up sits only 3 points under 50.
language_note: HC Andersen Capital's Danish preview (inderes.dk, 1 Oct) carried the H2 arithmetic (12-40% y/y adj. EBITDA growth needed; H1 = 40% of the midpoint) and the Q3-or-Q4 hardware timing. The English company releases give the inputs but not that framing.

HC Andersen Capital's Danish Q2 comments carried the consensus figures (revenue EURm 58.8, adj. EBITDA EURm 8.6, implied margin 14.6%) that establish the 26% Q2 miss. The English release does not state the bar.
